summary.headline: Mahindra Logistics Q2 FY27 PAT rose to INR26 crore (from a INR10 crore loss) and MESPL (Rivigo) turned EBITDA-positive at INR2.3 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 24% YoY to INR2,095 crore and EBITDA rose to INR124 crore (5.9% margin, up 90 bps YoY). Contract logistics (about 80% of revenue) grew 28% with EBITDA of INR115 crore, while gross margin stayed at 10.1% consolidated (up 40 bps QoQ). MESPL (Rivigo) posted its first EBITDA-positive quarter, and management pivoted the last-mile business from a no-loss to a growth strategy. Freight forwarding revenue fell 44% YoY on leadership transition, and a tech transformation project was approved for start around Q4 FY27.

vs loss of INR10 crore in Q2 FY26; vs INR25 crore in Q1 FY27
vs minus INR210 crore in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR308 crore (cash INR363 crore, debt INR55 crore)

segments.name: Contract logistics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,688 crore (+28% YoY vs INR1,317 crore); EBITDA INR115 crore vs INR89 crore. Gross margin grew 20% YoY; vacant space cut to 5% of June 2025 levels.

segments.name: MESPL (Rivigo, B2B express)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR169 crore (+69% YoY); EBITDA INR2.3 crore vs minus INR9 crore in Q2 FY26, first EBITDA-positive quarter. QoQ improvement was more yield-led than volume-led.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Revenue INR119 crore (+33% YoY vs INR90 crore); EBITDA INR3.4 crore vs INR2.1 crore. Management says gross margin grew 19% YoY; B2B is the majority of the mix.

segments.name: Last-mile delivery (LMD)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR68 crore, down 23% YoY from INR88 crore by choice; EBITDA INR1.6 crore vs INR0.4 crore; gross margin up 18.6% YoY. Strategy shifted from no-loss to growth; YoY growth expected from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Freight forwarding
segments.commentary: Revenue INR50.6 crore (+12% QoQ, down 44% YoY); EBITDA INR1.7 crore, down only INR0.5 crore YoY. H2 FY27 described as a build phase, with real delivery expected in FY28.

guidance_outlook: Contract logistics gross margin: target of about 100 bps improvement from exit of FY26 (about 11% FY26 level per analyst framing); management clarified this is a medium-term target, not two to four quarters.
Capex for FY27 about INR110 crore (INR100 crore plus or minus INR10 crore); roughly half spent in H1, mostly in contract logistics and the 2x2 car-carrier JV.
MESPL: next milestone is PAT positivity; no formal timeline given, described as a multi-year growth story with continued investment in network and hubs.
Growth now targeted from the LMD business and from new business wins, with an internal target to grow new business wins 3.5x versus last year; H1 is running ahead of that.
Festive-season flex-capacity costs in Q3 expected to recur, as in prior years.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex about INR110 crore (INR100 crore plus or minus INR10 crore); H1 spend about half, per management.
Capex mainly in contract logistics and in the 2x2 car-carrier JV serving Mahindra auto and tractor business.
Board approved a business transformation project (new tech platform for MESPL and MLL) on 23 Oct 2026; execution to start around Q4 FY27; investment amount not disclosed.
MESPL is adding real estate and hubs to handle higher capacity and is expanding its pin-code coverage.
Standalone balance sheet debt-free since September 2025; consolidated debt INR55 crore, mainly vehicle loans under the asset-right model.
demand_pricing: Contract logistics growth driven by new client additions and higher wallet share with existing customers; e-commerce, manufacturing, telecom and last-mile cited as strong verticals.

Fuel cost increase of INR8.10 per litre-equivalent (as stated) was fully passed through; manpower cost pressure (including PF wage-ceiling change from INR15,000 to INR25,000) is only partly passed through because many contracts lack pass-through clauses.
MESPL: yield-led QoQ improvement from selective calibration actions; management expects volume-led growth going forward through network expansion.
M&M share of consolidated revenue about 60% (58% in FY26); management says there is no internal target to reduce M&M share.
Monsoon was 14% below LPA nationally, unevenly distributed across states; management says overall FY27 plan is intact.

qa_highlights.question: How should the steady-state EBITDA margin of MESPL be thought of, versus a peer at 10-12%, given possible network investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no explicit guidance. Next milestone is PAT positivity, with full visibility on the path; MESPL is a multi-year, decade-long story with continued investment after PAT positivity.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the sequential contract logistics gross margin improvement only 30 bps given fuel pass-through and onboarding?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel pass-through was fully completed and reflected in the 30 bps gain. Manpower costs are not fully passed through, and new costs (e.g., PF slab change) add pressure; the 100 bps gross margin improvement target is reaffirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Was there capacity build-up for the festive/e-commerce peak, and what is the tech platform investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Flex sites were added for peak, with 3-4 days' notice from customers; these costs recur each Q3. Tech project approved by Board today; amount not disclosed; details to be shared once execution starts around Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Clarify whether the 100 bps margin improvement is gross or EBITDA, and from what base.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 100 bps target is at the gross margin level, measured from the exit rate of FY26 rather than the full-year FY26 average.

qa_highlights.question: Key growth drivers for the next 2-3 years, and any remaining cost levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth from new clients, wallet share, e-commerce and LMD; cost control largely played out, so growth is the main lever now. New business wins are running ahead of the 3.5x internal target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for LMD, freight forwarding and mobility, and their capital employed?
qa_highlights.answer: LMD is moving to growth; freight forwarding is in a build phase in H2 FY27 with results expected in FY28 and zero capex; mobility B2B has long-term contracts and B2C is limited to Delhi. Capital employed is low and returns exceed the ROCE threshold, per the CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Is the M&M share of revenue set to fall?
qa_highlights.answer: No internal target to reduce M&M share; M&M share is about 60%, and the aim is to win 100% of M&M business.

risks_watch: Contract logistics gross margin (10.1% consolidated) must improve by about 100 bps over the medium term; manpower cost pass-through remains incomplete.
Festive-season flex staffing costs in Q3 FY27 and possible volume spillover for MESPL.
Freight forwarding revenue down 44% YoY; geopolitical disruption and high spot container rates are delaying new contracts.
MESPL needs to convert EBITDA positivity into PAT positivity while funding network expansion and the new tech platform.
Concentration on M&M (about 60% of revenue) and on automotive and manufacturing verticals, which management acknowledges can be cyclical.
Monsoon shortfall (14% below LPA) and uneven regional impact.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the turnaround, especially MESPL EBITDA positivity and the balance sheet, but cautious and somewhat evasive on margin timelines and tech investment amounts. Management repeatedly stressed that margin targets are medium-term and declined to quantify MESPL margins or the tech spend.
